content_md:
Agents are getting really powerful, even if they are not necessarily consistent.

I'm testing an agent orchestrator (a 'Claw variant), with a fair amount of hype on X due to its security approach. I won't say which one it is, but its promises are distinctive.

---

I gave it a narrowly-scoped MCP server and login credentials, and asked it:

> please check my email

Note that I had to provide my credentials in plaintext in one big `.env` file, with each MCP service in its own block.

- the agent got stuck with my specified service, so fell back to `mcporter`

- it tested lots of things, including unrelated credentials I had provided for Brave Web Search API to use with a Brave Web Search MCP

- **it "Found a generic IMAP/SMTP MCP server", installed it, and tried a variety of connection strings and env vars with permutations of my credentials**

- it slurped my inbox AND archived folders, and read back to me in plaintext (*i.e.*, shared with my LLM provider) all the metadata

- it helpfully offered to do more stuff

---

Sandboxing doesn'
